theme: Unit 21 review, Law, Gospel & Church Life, Galatians, Corinthians
memoryText: I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Paul wrote these words in the middle of an argument about justification, but they are as personal as anything in his letters. They are the unit’s key.

“I have been crucified with Christ.” Paul speaks of a past event with present effect. When Christ died, those who are in him died with him. The old self, the power of sin, and the curse of the law all came to an end at the cross.

“It is no longer I who live.” The self-centered life, the one that lives for its own glory, has been put to death. This is not the loss of personality but of the old master.

“But Christ who lives in me.” The risen Christ now lives in the believer by his Spirit. He is not just a teacher to be imitated or a debt-payer to be thanked, but the life within us.

The rest of the verse, which you should read, says: “And the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.” We live by trusting him, and the basis is his love and his sacrifice.

This verse answers legalism, which says do more. It answers license, which says do what you want. The answer is union: Christ’s death is mine and Christ’s life is mine.

When you feel the pull of self-reliance or of sin, say this verse. You are not alone, and you are not what you were.
unitRecap: You have read Galatians, 1 Corinthians, and 2 Corinthians, three letters that show the gospel at work in churches. In Galatians, Paul defended the gospel against those who added the law to faith: there is no other gospel, a person is justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the law, Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us, and in Christ we are adopted as sons and heirs. We walk by the Spirit, bear his fruit, and boast only in the cross. In 1 Corinthians, you saw a messy, gifted church corrected by the cross: the word of the cross is the power of God, ministers are servants and stewards, the church is God’s temple, and Christians use their freedom in love. You studied the Lord’s Supper as the meal that proclaims the Lord’s death until he comes, spiritual gifts as given by one Spirit for the common good of one body, and love as the more excellent way. Chapter 15 gave the gospel of first importance and the hope of the resurrection of Christ and of the dead. In 2 Corinthians, you saw comfort in affliction, the new covenant ministry of the Spirit, the treasure in jars of clay, the new creation, the ministry of reconciliation, the grace of giving, and the sufficiency of grace in weakness. Doctrinal pauses covered adoption, the Lord’s Supper, spiritual gifts, the resurrection of Christ, the resurrection of the dead, and death and the intermediate state. Psalms 33, 62, 111, 112, and 133 sang of God’s word, rest in God alone, remembering his works, generosity, and unity.

reviewQuestions.question: What is the “different gospel” Paul is writing against in Galatians?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Read Galatians 1:6-9 and 2:15-21. What was added to faith in Christ, and why does Paul say that adding anything destroys the gospel? Where might a version of this temptation appear today?

reviewQuestions.question: What does “justification by faith” mean practically?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Consider Galatians 2:16, 3:1-14, and 5:1-6. How does it change your view of yourself, your failures, your obedience, and other people when you rest on Christ’s finished work instead of your own performance?

reviewQuestions.question: Why does Paul say “I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ and him crucified”?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Look at 1 Corinthians 1:18-2:5. What was wrong with the Corinthians’ approach to wisdom and leaders? Why is the cross both foolish to the world and the power of God?

reviewQuestions.question: What does the resurrection of 1 Corinthians 15 have to do with everyday Christian living?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Read 1 Corinthians 15:12-20 and 15:50-58. If Christ is raised, what follows for how we face death, suffering, our bodies, and our work for the Lord?

prayerPrompts: Thank God for the gospel in Galatians and Corinthians.
Tell him where you have seen law and gospel, grace and church life, together.
Ask him to keep the unit verse before you.
